title: Bartender
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Ryū Sasakura, a prize-winning young bartender back from training in France, runs a hidden Ginza bar, Eden Hall, and later works at the Hotel Cardinal at the urging of the owner's granddaughter Miwa. Each episode brings a troubled customer, from a struggling marriage to a disgraced politician, and Ryū reads them and serves 'the right drink at the right time', leading them to reflect and decide what to do. A 21-volume episodic seinen 'healing' manga full of cocktail lore.
life_message: Attentive hospitality and an honest moment of reflection can help people face their troubles.

content.note: Alcohol and cocktails in every chapter (MangaUpdates Alcohol, Bar); Wikipedia: drinking never shown as a problem; a critic says it romanticizes the bar.
Customers' stress, grief and burdens eased (Wikipedia).
Drinking presented as a path to clarity and healing (Wikipedia).
Named liquors and cocktail recipes; educational bar trivia (MangaUpdates Educational).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Quality of life and emotional healing (Reverse Thieves).

folkways.japan: Reflects Japanese omotenashi (anticipatory hospitality), shokunin craft devotion and Ginza bar culture where drinking with colleagues is socially normal.

delivery.evidence: Each chapter resolves a problem through the right drink (Wikipedia); critic Ink says it romanticizes the bar.
delivery.note: Wikipedia notes drinking is never presented as a problem, so the case against alcohol does not appear.

winners_losers: Troubled patrons find clarity and Ryū grows in his career; there are no villains; sympathy is with the bartender's craft.
